'''James Victor Uspensky''' ({{langx|ru|Яков Викторович Успенский|translit=Yakov Viktorovich Uspensky}}; April 29, 1883 – January 27, 1947) was a Russian and American [[mathematician]] notable for writing ''Theory of Equations''.<ref name=JV>J. V. Uspensky (1948). Theory of Equations. Pp. vii. 353. New York: McGraw-Hill Book Co.</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Book Review: Theory of Equations, by J. V. Uspensky |author=Kenneth May|journal=Popular Astronomy|volume=57|year=1949|pages=46|bibcode=1949PA.....57...46M}} [https://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1949PA.....57...46M].</ref>

==Biography==
Uspensky graduated from the [[University of St. Petersburg]] in 1906 and received his doctorate from the [[University of St. Petersburg]] in 1910. He was a member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] from 1921.<ref name="Royden 1988">Royden (1988).</ref>

Uspensky joined the faculty of [[Stanford University]] in 1929-30 and 1930–31 as acting professor of mathematics. He was professor of mathematics at Stanford from 1931 until his death.<ref name="Royden 1988"/> Uspensky was the one who kept alive [[Vincent's theorem]] of 1834 and 1836, carrying the torch (so to speak) from Serret.<ref>[http://www.apmath.spbu.ru/ru/misc/uspenskii.html Uspensky's biography ] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201007013013/http://www.apmath.spbu.ru/ru/misc/uspenskii.html |date=2020-10-07 }} (in Russian).</ref>
